rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression prevention
rows.verified: Work-related violence includes verbal abuse and threats as well as physical attacks.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression prevention
rows.verified: Employers must assess violence and aggression risks and put suitable controls in place.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression prevention
rows.verified: Risk controls can include safer work design, staffing, communication, training and arrangements for summoning assistance.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression prevention
rows.verified: Lone workers, new starters, trainees and other vulnerable workers may face increased violence risk.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression prevention
rows.verified: Employers should record and learn from incidents, including near misses and patterns of aggressive behaviour.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression prevention
rows.verified: Workers should receive information and training relevant to the violence risks in their work.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression prevention
rows.verified: After an incident, employers should support workers who may be physically or psychologically affected.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression prevention
rows.verified: Workers should cooperate with agreed controls and report concerns or incidents through workplace procedures.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression prevention
rows.verified: Violence risk depends on sector, task, location, lone working, client behaviour, staffing, communication, training and emergency support.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression prevention
rows.verified: HSE violence evidence is workplace-, task-, worker-, customer-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level assault probability.

rows.source: HSE occupational-asthma prevention and health surveillance
rows.verified: Occupational asthma can result from exposure to respiratory sensitisers such as flour dust, wood dust or isocyanates.

rows.source: HSE occupational-asthma prevention and health surveillance
rows.verified: Once a worker becomes sensitised, further exposure at relatively low levels may trigger an asthma attack.

rows.source: HSE occupational-asthma prevention and health surveillance
rows.verified: Symptoms can include wheezing, coughing, chest tightness and severe shortness of breath, sometimes appearing hours after exposure.

rows.source: HSE occupational-asthma prevention and health surveillance
rows.verified: COSHH requires employers to assess exposure and prevent it where reasonably practicable or otherwise control it adequately.

rows.source: HSE occupational-asthma prevention and health surveillance
rows.verified: Substitution, local exhaust ventilation, supervision, training and correct work practices are recognised control measures.

rows.source: HSE occupational-asthma prevention and health surveillance
rows.verified: Controls must be maintained in effective working order and their performance checked.

rows.source: HSE occupational-asthma prevention and health surveillance
rows.verified: Workers exposed or likely to be exposed to asthmagens should receive suitable health surveillance.

rows.source: HSE occupational-asthma prevention and health surveillance
rows.verified: Reportable occupational asthma includes cases linked to significant or regular exposure to known respiratory sensitisers.

rows.source: HSE occupational-asthma prevention and health surveillance
rows.verified: Occupational-asthma risk depends on sensitiser, concentration, route, exposure duration, controls, susceptibility, surveillance and diagnosis.

rows.source: HSE occupational-asthma prevention and health surveillance
rows.verified: HSE asthma evidence is substance-, process-, workplace-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
